completion_data.completion_summary: Resolved postflight-sapience-notes.sh's Sapience project key once per completed task instead of once per note, by duplicating sapience-remember.sh's PROJECT-KEY RESOLUTION block directly into the calling script and forwarding the result as --project-key to every per-note call; an unlinked repo's behavior is unchanged (zero GETs, no flag forwarded). Added two new regression cases (linked: one GET, same key on every call; unlinked: zero GETs, no flag) to test-postflight-sapience-notes.sh, bringing it to 41/41 passing; test-sapience-remember.sh's Phase 2 flag contract remains 11/11.

memory_candidates.content: When a test suite's own declared file_scope restricts an edit to one script and its test file, but the correct fix conceptually belongs partly in a sibling script that is out of scope, duplicating the sibling's relevant block directly (with a header note explaining why) is the sanctioned move in this codebase -- it mirrors the pattern the sibling's own PROJECT-KEY RESOLUTION / sapience-worktree-checkout-resolution blocks already use for the same reason, rather than widening file_scope mid-phase.

verify-touched.sh's run-all.sh invocation resolves each selected test suite's script-under-test via the deployed .claude/ mirror first (deploy-tree-first), with no CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE override of its own -- so a verify-touched.sh run taken while an extension's deployed tree is known-stale (per the dispatch's own <deploy-freshness-context>) silently exercises the OLD deployed copy, not the edited source-store copy, even though it reports a clean pass. The authoritative check of a source-store-only change, before its next redeploy, is a direct `CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store bash <source-store-suite>.sh` invocation, not the batch-deferred verify-touched.sh probe.

sapience_notes.subject: postflight-sapience-notes.sh resolve-once pass-through for the linked-repo project key
sapience_notes.value: postflight-sapience-notes.sh now resolves this repo's Sapience project key at most once per completed task (duplicating sapience-remember.sh's own PROJECT-KEY RESOLUTION block rather than modifying that script, which was out of this phase's declared file_scope) and forwards it to every per-note sapience-remember.sh call as --project-key, cutting a linked repo's GET /v1/people/projects count from one-per-note to one-per-task. An unlinked repo's behavior (no .sapience/project.json) is unchanged: zero GETs, no --project-key forwarded.

sapience_notes.subject: Resolve-once degrade path is exact only on the success branch
sapience_notes.value: When postflight-sapience-notes.sh's own project-key resolution fails (binding present but the GET fails or matches no entry), it omits --project-key from every per-note call, so each sapience-remember.sh invocation still attempts its own per-call fallback GET (its pre-existing behavior for that one call). The 'one GET per task' guarantee is therefore exact for the success path (what the plan's own Verification criterion tests) and a best-effort improvement -- one issue row recorded once, rather than per-note silence -- on the degrade path, not a hard GET-count bound there.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh does not exercise a source-store-only change ahead of redeploy
sapience_notes.value: verify-touched.sh's run-all.sh invocation resolves each test suite's script-under-test deploy-tree-first with no CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE override, so running it while an extension's deployed tree is flagged stale reports a clean pass by exercising the OLD deployed copy, not the edited source-store copy. Confirmed live on this task: the scoped verify-touched.sh probe reported 98 passed/0 failed while the sapience extension's deployed tree was still stale, whereas CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store bash test-postflight-sapience-notes.sh was the call that actually exercised this phase's new code.

sapience_notes.subject: Repo-root resolution in a postflight script must come from the script's own location, not cwd
sapience_notes.value: postflight-sapience-notes.sh resolves PROJECT_ROOT via common_repo_root("$SCRIPT_DIR", 2) rather than from cwd, matching sapience-remember.sh's identical convention, because its two production call sites (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, reconcile-task-status.sh) invoke it by an absolute, ${SKILL_REPO_ROOT}/${PROJECT_ROOT}-qualified path without guaranteeing cwd is the repo root at that point.
